title: Ada and the Wreck
premise: Riverboat captain Lior Oyelaran is hired to resupply a survey expedition that has gone silent in the flooded headwaters of the Sable River. They find the camp wrecked, the scientists dead or scattered, and a sealed crate the survivors will do anything to protect—evidence of something in the river that shouldn't exist. Hunted by the company that funded the expedition, Lior must choose between delivering the crate for a fortune or burning it to keep their found crew safe, and in the end scuttles their own beloved boat to destroy the evidence and buy the survivors a new life ashore.
about_author: M. M. Pemberton is the pen name of a former merchant-marine radio operator who spent a decade on inland waterways before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people whose homes are the vehicles that carry them.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A portrait of the riverboat Ada and her ragtag crew running cargo on the Sable, establishing the rhythms, debts, and quiet loyalties of life afloat. A lucrative contract arrives: resupply a survey expedition upriver that has stopped answering its radio. Beat: restlessness—the ache of a life measured only in distance.

chapters.title: The Last Clear Channel
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, with interludes of the expedition's final garbled radio transmissions. The Ada fights rising water and hostile checkpoints as the crew debates turning back. Engineer Sefi argues the money is a trap; deckhand Tomas wants the payday. Beat: unease deepening into dread as the river narrows and the silence ahead grows louder.

chapters.title: What the Flood Kept
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. They reach the expedition camp: tents shredded, boats sunk, one survivor—Dr. Imka Voss—half-mad, guarding a sealed steel crate. She refuses to say what killed the others, only that it came up with the flood. Beat: horror and the first irrevocable choice, taking Voss and the crate aboard.

chapters.title: Company Men
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A company gunboat hails them at a fueling station; the expedition's funder, Meridian Consolidated, wants its 'property' recovered intact. Lior lies smoothly, but Tomas realizes the captain is already planning something and feels shut out. Beat: the crew's belonging fractures under the weight of a secret.

chapters.title: The Crate
chapters.summary: Sefi's POV. Voss finally opens up: the crate holds samples proving the flood released something alive in the deep channels—something Meridian caused with its upstream drilling. Sefi, who trusts machines over people, believes her. Beat: reluctant faith; Sefi chooses the crew over the truth's safety.

chapters.title: Deadwater
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The gunboat herds the Ada into a deadwater bend and boards. A tense standoff; Lior surrenders the crate's location to save Tomas, whom they take hostage. Beat: the price of survival made literal—Lior trades truth for a life and hates how easily they did it.

chapters.title: Sandbar's Mood
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV, captive on the gunboat. Tomas learns Meridian plans to sink the Ada with 'evidence' aboard once the crate is secured, and escapes at night, swimming the channel Voss warned was unsafe. Beat: defiance; Tomas stops being a passenger in his own life.

chapters.title: Everything the River Owes
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Reunion in a storm; the crew, now fully a family, plans the impossible—use Lior's encyclopedic knowledge of the sandbars to run the gunboat aground and take the crate back. Beat: belonging forged in crisis; every crew member contributes the thing they're best at.

chapters.title: The Wreck
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The climax: Lior deliberately wrecks the Ada on a shoal to block the channel, trapping the gunboat while the crate is cracked open and its contents destroyed in the flood. Voss nearly drowns saving Sefi; Tomas pilots the lifeboat. Beat: sacrifice—the price of survival is the home itself.

chapters.title: Ashore
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, months later. Meridian's cover-up collapses quietly; the crew, scattered and untraceable, reunites in a river town where Voss is teaching and Tomas is building a new boat. Lior, who never wanted roots, plants one. Beat: resolution—belonging was never the river; it was the people all along.
